subject: Apportioned collections & VAT routing for ACME — invoice splitting and cost-center mapping
messages:
From: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@acmecorp.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: AP Team <ap@acmecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Billing setup for Redwood services — multi-entity split and VAT details

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week. ACME is ready to move forward but we need the invoice/payment flow to match our internal cost allocation and VAT reporting requirements. A couple of specifics: 

- We have three internal cost centers that must each receive an allocation line on the invoice (C-ENG, C-MKT, C-SLS). Our ERP needs a mapping string (e.g., C-ENG|12345) on the invoice line.
- We need invoices issued from the relevant legal entity so VAT numbers and invoicing address match the receiving entity (UK entity + two EU subsidiaries).
- AP prefers a single remittance where possible, but we can do separate wires if Redwood needs separate beneficiary accounts.
- PO attached: acme_po_20261117.pdf. Terms Net 30.

Can your billing team confirm whether Redwood can: 1) issue per-entity invoices with VAT registration on each invoice; 2) include cost-center metadata on line items; and 3) accept a single combined payment and automatically apply allocations?

Best,
Sasha Patel
Head of Procurement
ACME Corp

--

- You need per-entity VAT accuracy on invoices.
- Cost-center codes must be present on invoice lines for ERP mapping.
- AP would prefer a single remittance if we can auto-apply allocations.

Marcus — can you propose the approach (separate invoices vs single invoice with split lines) and whether we can support automatic allocation on remittance? Also include whether we need separate beneficiary accounts per legal entity.

Neha — FYI for deal economics and whether any discounts/credits require being tied to a specific invoice/entity.

Sasha — we should be able to get you a sample invoice layout and the remittance instructions by EOD tomorrow.

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:07:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Billing setup for Redwood services — multi-entity split and VAT details

Lauren / Neha — thanks. Below are the pragmatic options with tradeoffs and recommended implementation steps.

Option A — Separate invoices from each Redwood legal entity
- We can issue discrete invoices from UK/EU legal entities if the contractual account is segmented by entity. Each invoice shows the issuing entity name, VAT reg no., billing address and local bank details.
- Pros: Clean VAT paperwork per entity; matches ACME accounting lines if you require entity-level purchase orders.
- Cons: Requires ACME to make multiple payments (unless you want to route a single payment and we do manual apply).

Option B — Single consolidated invoice with apportioned lines and entity tags (recommended for ACME)
- Single PDF invoice showing line-level allocation: each line includes service description, amount, currency, VAT rate, and a custom metadata column for cost-center (e.g., "C-ENG|12345"). We include a header section listing entity VAT registrations and an invoice footer indicating how amounts are allocated across entities.
- Pros: AP-friendly (one payment), simpler remittance.
- Cons: For VAT filing, you must accept that the invoice originates from Redwood's master billing entity and we apply intercompany accounting entries behind the scenes. We'll include VAT registration numbers per entity for your records and provide a monthly clearing statement.

Payment routing / remittance handling
- We can accept a single payment to our clearing account and auto-apply to the consolidated invoice if ACME provides remittance advice with line allocations. Alternatively, you can send separate wires to each legal entity bank account; we can provide beneficiary details per entity.

Sample data fields we can embed on invoice lines:
- description | quantity | unit price | line total | VAT rate | cost_center_code (freeform) | entity_tag (ENT-UK / ENT-EU1 / ENT-EU2)

VAT treatment notes
- If an invoice is issued by a single Redwood entity but amounts are attributable to other entities, we will provide supporting intercompany memos and VAT registration numbers to assist your reclaim/filing. For reverse-charge scenarios we will mark the line accordingly and include required wording.

Action items
1) Decide on Option A or B (ACME preference).
2) If Option B, provide exact cost-center string format and ERP mapping examples.
3) Redwood to send sample split invoice (PDF + XLS) and remittance instructions.

Bank details (stub)
- Redwood Clearing Account — Redwood Inference LP | Bank: ExampleBank | IBAN: GB00REDD00000000000000 (live details provided in secure doc)

I'll prepare a sample invoice and an XLS mapping tomorrow.

-marcus
Marcus Lin
Finance Director, Billing Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Sasha — thanks for the details and PO. From a sales/contracting perspective:

- Deal reference RWI-ACME-2026Q4-42 will remain under the master subscription. Discounts offered in the proposal are applied at the account level and can be reflected on the consolidated invoice (Option B) or split across invoices (Option A) as required.
- If you choose Option A, finance will need explicit allocation of the agreed discount per entity.
- For timing: we can close the billing setup and start billing against the PO once we have the chosen approach + cost-center mappings.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you want to walk through ERP mapping with Marcus.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Billing setup for Redwood services — multi-entity split and VAT details

Thanks everyone — ACME prefers Option B (single consolidated invoice) provided that:

1) Each invoice line contains our cost-center token exactly as C-ENG|12345, etc.
2) The invoice includes a small table mapping amounts to Redwood entity tags we receive (ENT-UK / ENT-EU1 / ENT-EU2) so our tax team has visibility.
3) You provide a sample PDF + XLS and remittance instructions before go-live.

We are fine with payment to a single clearing account as long as you provide a monthly clearing statement and the line-level mapping so our treasury team can reconcile.

Please send the sample invoice and remittance instructions and we'll confirm PO acceptance.

Regards,
Sasha Patel
Head of Procurement
ACME Corp
